caption:
Stanford physicists (Safavi-Naeini lab) directly watched single phonons, the quantum packets of vibration, jump between energy levels in a mechanical resonator in real time. Quantum jumps: ions 1986, photons 2007, sound 2026. Science, 17 Sept 2026, DOI 10.1126/science.aeh7535.

#physics #quantum #science #stanford
voiceover_script: Sound does not fade away smoothly. At the smallest scale, it jumps. Sound is vibration, and vibration is energy. At the quantum level that energy comes in packets called phonons. A phonon can only sit on fixed energy steps, never in between. Physicists at Stanford, in the Safavi-Naeini lab, built a tiny mechanical resonator that rings for about two milliseconds, and watched single phonons jump between those steps in real time. It is the first direct real-time observation of a quantum jump in sound. Quantum jumps were seen in ions in 1986, in photons in 2007, and now in sound. The result is in the journal Science, published on the seventeenth of September. Source in the caption.
